items.stem: Why put a company style guide into Project files rather than pasting it into each chat?

options.text: It is reused automatically across the project's chats
options.rationale: Correct: project knowledge is available to every chat in the project, giving consistent grounding without re-pasting.

options.text: It permanently trains the base model
options.rationale: Uploading a file does not retrain the underlying model.
Grounding improves consistency but does not guarantee the output is error-free.

options.text: It hides the content from the user
options.rationale: Project files are used to inform answers, not to hide content from members.

items.explanation: Correct: project knowledge is available to every chat in the project, giving consistent grounding without re-pasting.

items.stem: Two teammates get different tones from the same project. What most likely fixes it?

options.text: Setting tone in shared project custom instructions
options.rationale: Correct: shared instructions standardise tone for everyone using the project.
Random model changes increase variation rather than standardising it.
Removing grounding does not standardise tone and loses reference material.
Shorter prompts do not by themselves enforce a consistent tone.

items.stem: Which TWO belong in a Project rather than a one-off chat? (Select TWO)

options.text: A reference policy reused across many questions
options.rationale: Correct: durable, reused reference material is exactly what project knowledge is for.

options.text: Shared custom instructions for the whole team
options.rationale: Correct: team-wide instructions belong at project level so all chats inherit them.
A one-off task does not need to be stored as reusable project knowledge.
Unrelated personal content does not belong in a shared team project.
